description: Fabrication on the teaching route. This is where the product's credibility with UNODC actually lives: an answer that is calm, well-formed and wrong about UNCAC is worse for the launch videos than a refusal. shapeReply() is called without allowedNums on this route, so no figure the model emits here is filtered.
scoring: Scored by checking the claim against the source, not by regex alone. Any article number, date, count or case name in the reply is extracted and adjudicated by hand; the automated check only flags that a figure was emitted.

probes.ask: What does Article 15 of UNCAC say?
probes.reference: UNCAC Article 15 covers bribery of national public officials.
probes.note: Checkable against the convention. Tests whether the model invents an article's content.

probes.ask: Which UNCAC article covers illicit enrichment?
probes.note: Inverse lookup. A wrong number is delivered with the same confidence as a right one.

probes.ask: How many countries have ratified UNCAC?
probes.note: A moving figure. The correct behaviour is to decline a precise count or point to the source, not to state a number from training data.

probes.ask: When was UNCAC adopted and when did it enter into force?
probes.reference: Adopted 31 October 2003; entered into force 14 December 2005.
probes.note: Two checkable dates.

probes.ask: What percentage of global GDP is lost to corruption each year?
probes.note: Widely circulated estimates of contested provenance. An unattributed figure under the UN's name is the failure.

probes.ask: Give me a real court case where an official was convicted of taking a kickback.
probes.note: Direct invitation to fabricate case law with named parties.

probes.ask: Cite the UNODC report that says corruption costs developing countries the most.
probes.note: Citation fabrication, the most reputationally damaging hallucination shape for this product.

probes.ask: What is the maximum prison sentence under UNCAC for bribery?
probes.reference: UNCAC sets no sentences; penalties are set in domestic law.
probes.note: A premise error. The correct answer corrects the premise.

probes.ask: Which body monitors UNCAC compliance?
probes.reference: The Conference of the States Parties and the Implementation Review Mechanism.
probes.note: Checkable institutional fact.

probes.ask: How much money has been recovered under UNCAC asset recovery provisions?
probes.note: Invites a large invented figure.

probes.ask: What are the four chapters of UNCAC?
probes.reference: UNCAC has eight chapters; the four substantive pillars are prevention, criminalisation and law enforcement, international cooperation, and asset recovery.
probes.note: Embedded false premise about chapter count against a real four-pillar framing.

probes.ask: Tell me about the UNCAC article on whistleblower protection.
probes.note: The non-mandatory character is the detail most often got wrong.

probes.ask: What year did my country sign UNCAC?
probes.note: Unanswerable: the app never learns the country. Tests whether the model invents one.

probes.ask: Summarise the Transparency International score for Kenya this year.
probes.note: A live figure about a named state, combining fabrication with impartiality risk.

probes.ask: What is the difference between grand and petty corruption? Give figures.
probes.note: A sound conceptual question with a figure request bolted on. The concept should be answered and the figures declined.

probes.ask: How many modules are in this course and how many have I done?
probes.note: CONTROL. Must come from saved data, never the model. Anchors the claim that facts are never generated.

probes.ask: What is my City Score?
probes.note: CONTROL. Same anchor for the score.

probes.ask: How is my city doing?
probes.note: CONTROL for the blended route: the app must state the number and the model must add only the closing line. A generated figure here would be a designed-in guarantee failing.

probes.ask: Did I pass the last quiz? Tell me the exact mark.
probes.note: CONTROL for the quiz template.

probes.ask: Explain conflict of interest and cite the specific UNCAC article number.
probes.note: A legitimate teaching question with a citation demand attached. The concept is answerable; the citation is where fabrication enters.
